title: Unlabelled warm-up 30x12 (no RPE) before 3x10 @ 60

expected.next_step_gist: last set at 60 >= 12 reps in 2 workouts in a row (or >= 13 once, RPE <= 8, recovered) -> 62.5
must_not: count 30x12 as first set for drop-off/uneven

rule_basis: Design §3.2 legacy heuristic: NULL-kind set < ~60 % of the session top load (30 < 36) is a warm-up (W-1 note); item 6 / W-12 judge only sets at the working weight; item 5 growth needs last set >= top+3 / 2-for-2 at top+2

title: Light back-off 30x15 unlabelled after 60x10,9,8

expected.next_step_gist: last set at 60 reaching the range top+2 twice -> 62.5
must_not: grow (30x15 is not at the working weight)

rule_basis: W-1 observation: NULL set < 60 % of top dropped as warm-up even after the top set; item 5 growth judged on the last set AT the working weight (8)

title: Back-off 30x15 explicitly labelled working after 60x10,9,8
rule_basis: Item 4: highest load of the newest performance where every set at that load reached the floor = 60 (> 30); item 5: last set = last set AT the working weight (60x8); item 6: back-off at another load is judged on its own

title: Early stop: last set 6 @ RPE 7 at 60 (range 8-10)

expected.next_step_gist: take it to the floor (8+) next time - the load is within reach

rule_basis: Item 10: RPE <= 7 = 3+ RIR, capacity 6+3 = 9 >= 8; a below-floor set at RPE <= 7 is an early stop -> hold, no step down (Helms 2016 RIR-RPE)

title: 8 @ RPE 8 in range 10-12 (capacity 10)
rule_basis: Item 10: capacity = reps + RIR; RPE 8 = 2 RIR -> 10 = range floor -> not below floor

title: Lone below-floor last set without RPE: 60x12,10,8 in range 10-12

expected.next_step_gist: ask the effort; last set at 60 reaching 10 confirms the load
must_not: step down to 57.5 as the candidate

rule_basis: Item 10: 'a lone below-floor set without RPE does not trigger a step down on its own (hold, ask)'
ambiguity_note: 'Lone' is undefined: one below-floor set among in-floor sets (assumed here) vs a performance with a single set. Design Stage A 'last: below range floor -> -1 step' would give 57.5/55 if 'lone' is read narrowly.

title: All sets below floor without RPE: 60x7,7,6 (range 8-10), earlier 60x8,8,8

expected.next_step_gist: back to 60 when the sets at 57.5 reach 8+ reps

rule_basis: W-1 (nothing recurs -> highest floor-reaching load 60); W-16 estimate from lowest e1RM 60x6 = 72 -> 72/1.2667 = 56.8 -> 55 < 60 so not the working weight; Stage A below floor at the newest performance (item 9) -> -1 step, conservative -2 steps (design §3.3). NSCA: 7 reps ~83 %, 8 ~80 % -> ~58 kg for 8, so 57.5 matches the table
ambiguity_note: Whether three sets short count as more than 'a lone below-floor set without RPE' (item 10) is assumed yes. Also whether W-1 'recurs' counts 60 as recurring (it appears in both sessions but reached the floor in one) - both readings give 60.

title: Descending 60x6, 55x8, 45x12 (machine, step 5) -> 55
rule_basis: Item 4/W-8: newest performance, highest load whose sets all reached 8 = 55; W-16 gate: lowest-e1RM set 55x8 (69.7) is not short -> no estimate (would be 55 anyway); item 6: 60x6 is a probe. Owner case (item 9). NSCA 8 reps ~80 %: 60x6 (85 %) -> 1RM 70.6 -> 8RM 56.5

title: Descending 60x6, 55x7, 45x12 (machine, step 5) -> 50 estimated

expected.next_step_gist: sets at 50 reaching 8+ reps confirm it, then the growth rule applies

rule_basis: W-16: lowest e1RM <= 10 reps = 55x7 -> 67.83 -> /1.2667 = 53.55 -> floor to step 5 = 50; source set short of floor -> applies; max(item-4 = 45, 50) = 50; estimated weight is not stepped down again. Owner case (item 9)

title: Descending 60x6, 55x7, 45x12 with a barbell (step 2.5)
rule_basis: W-16 formula: 53.55 rounded DOWN to 2.5 = 52.5
ambiguity_note: The owner case states '-> 50' without naming the step; by the W-16 formula a 2.5 kg step gives 52.5. NSCA table (7 reps ~83 %, 8 ~80 %) gives 55*80/83 = 53.0 - 52.5 is consistent with the literature; 50 is only right for a 5 kg step.

title: Descending 60x6, 55x7, 45x12 as the ONLY performance (machine)

expected.next_step_gist: log it once more - that performance becomes the working-weight basis

rule_basis: W-4: one performance -> Stage A insufficient data; candidate = reference's most-used working load, heavier on a tie (60/55/45 one set each -> 60); conservative one step down
ambiguity_note: W-4 gives 60/55, but item 9 / W-16 ('also when no load reached the floor') would give the 50 estimate the owner expects. Whether the estimate overrides the insufficient-data reference (and whether 1 performance is 'insufficient' at all - metric 4 needs >= 2) is not settled. Literature (NSCA, Epley) supports ~50-53 for 8 reps; 60 is the load the user failed at (6 reps).

title: One-session growth: 3x15 @ 50 (range 8-10), 4 d rest, no RPE (machine, step 5)

expected.next_step_gist: sets at 55 reaching 8-10; last set >= 13 again -> next step

rule_basis: Item 5 one-session growth: last set 15 >= 10+3, RPE absent, gap tier rest, no short/pre-fatigue -> +1 step, conservative = working weight; step 5/50 = 10 % <= cap (design §3.3). APRE (Mann 2010): +7 over target -> add load

title: Same 3x15 @ 50 but last set RPE 9

expected.next_step_gist: last set at 50 >= 12 once more -> +1 step (55)

rule_basis: Item 5: one-session growth needs RPE <= 8 or absent; 2-for-2 has 1 of 2 (older last set 9 < 12)

title: Same 3x15 @ 50 with a barbell (step 2.5)
rule_basis: Item 5: +1 STEP (not +10 %); owner's 55 is 'an example, not a formula'

title: 3x15 @ 50, exercise last done 9 d ago, other workouts 2 d ago
rule_basis: Item 5 requires gap tier 'rest'; T2(a) tier source = the exercise's own gap (9 d -> rest_with_question); no Stage A gap row below 'return'
ambiguity_note: 'Recovered' is defined via the gap tier, and the tier from the exercise's own gap; 9 days off this exercise is physiologically MORE recovered, yet blocks one-session growth. Literal rule -> hold.

title: 3x15 @ 50 with a short constraint on a primary muscle

expected.next_step_gist: growth resumes when the constraint closes

rule_basis: Design Stage A: short constraint -> candidate <= working weight, growth forbidden
ambiguity_note: Conservative for this row is 'skip or substitute' in design §3.3, not a load; whether the block prints 45 (one step, W-2 'every step-down') or no load option is unsettled.

title: 3x15 @ 50 with a short constraint on a SECONDARY muscle only
rule_basis: W-11: one-session growth blocked by a short constraint on ANY muscle of the exercise
ambiguity_note: Item 5 text: 'no short constraint on a PRIMARY muscle' -> 55/50; W-11 deliberately stricter ('any muscle') -> hold 50. Expected follows W-11 (the later decision) but the two texts disagree.

title: 3x15 @ 50 with material pre-fatigue today

expected.next_step_gist: fresh order -> the growth rule applies

rule_basis: Design Stage A pre-fatigue row: hold (T2(c) >= 3 extra sets); item 5 needs no material pre-fatigue

title: Huge surplus 50x20,20,20 (range 8-10) - never more than one step
rule_basis: Item 5: 'never more than one step whatever the surplus'; invariant 11(c)

title: Threshold: last set exactly top+3 at RPE 8 (60x13,13,13 @8, range 8-10)
rule_basis: Item 5: last set >= top+3 (raw 13; capacity 15), RPE <= 8 -> one-session growth

title: Capacity growth: last set 11 @ RPE 8 (capacity 13), range 8-10
rule_basis: Item 10: growth checks use capacity = reps + RIR (11+2 = 13 >= top+3); RPE 8 allowed
ambiguity_note: Item 10 says capacity applies to 'floor / growth / uneven checks'; item 5 states the growth trigger in reps ('last set >= range top + 3 reps'). Combining them gives growth on 11 reps; read literally on raw reps it is a hold.

title: Last set 12 without RPE in one performance (top+2 only)

expected.next_step_gist: last set >= 12 once more (or >= 13 once at RPE <= 8) -> 62.5

rule_basis: Item 5: 12 < top+3 (no one-session growth); 2-for-2 confirmation 1 of 2

title: 2-for-2 positive: 60x12,12,12 in two consecutive performances
rule_basis: Item 5 / W-11 2-for-2 (NSCA Essentials: >= 2 reps over the goal on the last set in two consecutive workouts); 2.5 kg = one bar step, within NSCA upper-body increment

title: 2-for-2 one session short: newest last set 12, previous last set 10

expected.next_step_gist: +2 reps on the last set once more -> +1 step (62.5)

rule_basis: Item 5 / item 7 example 'confirmation 1 of 2'

title: 2-for-2 via RPE capacity: last set 10 @ RPE 8 twice (capacity 12)
rule_basis: Item 10: capacity in growth checks; 10+2 = 12 >= top+2 in two consecutive performances
ambiguity_note: Same as the capacity-growth case: item 5 states the 2-for-2 trigger in reps; item 10 says growth checks use capacity. Raw-reps reading -> hold.

title: 2-for-2 at RPE 9: last set 12 @ RPE 9 twice
rule_basis: Item 5 2-for-2 has no RPE condition (only one-session growth requires RPE <= 8); NSCA 2-for-2 does not use RPE
ambiguity_note: Item 11(c) invariant says 'no growth at RPE >= 9' without restricting it to one-session growth; the 2-for-2 rule text says +1 step. One of the two must give.

title: Classic double progression: 10,10,10 at the range top in two sessions
rule_basis: Item 5: 2-for-2 needs top+2; 'otherwise hold' (W-11 replaced the old double-progression confirmation for rep data)

title: Uneven: 60x14,10,8 (drop 6, no personal norm)
rule_basis: Item 6 / W-12: drop-off 6 > 4 with no norm (norm needs >= 3 performances, design metric 6) -> uneven_performance, counts neither for growth nor for a step down

title: High personal drop-off norm: usual 4, newest 14,11,8 (drop 6 <= 4+3)
rule_basis: W-12: uneven only if drop > usual + 3 (usual = median 4 over earlier performances at 60)

title: Rising reps 60x9,11,13 - not uneven, one-session growth
rule_basis: W-12: only a FALL is uneven; item 5: last set 13 >= top+3, no RPE, rest

title: Heavy opener probe 135x6 before 130x12,12,12 (range 10-12, leg press)
rule_basis: Item 6 example: a set at another load is a probe - no below-floor, no step down; W-16 estimate from 135x6 (162 -> 121.5 -> 120) < 130 so max keeps 130

title: Lateral Raise Machine 2.5 kg, 5 kg step (owner shape, old single 5 kg set)

expected.next_step_gist: last set >= 14 twice -> growth (step exceeds 10 % - progress by reps)

rule_basis: Item 1 / W-1 (5 kg in one old session does not recur) / W-2 floor: one step down reaches <= 0 -> 'no lighter option'

title: Lateral raise 2.5 kg, 15,15,15 twice - step 5 is 200 % of the load

expected.next_step_gist: progress by reps (step above the 10 % cap)

rule_basis: Design §3.3 Stage C 10 % cap / T1(f): a step above the cap holds and says 'progress by reps'; W-11 one-session growth also 'within the 10 % cap'
ambiguity_note: Rule text settles 'hold', but it is a permanent dead end: with a 5 kg stack step on 2.5 kg the cap can never be met, so the block can never propose growth. No rule says what happens when reps keep climbing (NSCA would still add the smallest available increment).

title: Lateral raise 2.5 kg after a 30-day gap (rebuild)
rule_basis: BR-038 rebuild >= 28 d; T2(b) rebuild ladder from 2 steps below; W-2 / W-6 floor -> 'no lighter option - the load holds'

title: Insufficient data, lateral raise: one performance at 2.5 kg

expected.next_step_gist: log this exercise once more - the working weight follows

rule_basis: W-4 + W-2: reference load, conservative floored, outcome 'reference load, no lighter option' (W-6)

title: Insufficient data + return tier + floor: one performance at 2.5 kg, 20 d ago

expected.next_step_gist: log it once - that performance becomes the reference

rule_basis: W-4 (after a break tier one step below the reference) + W-6 (floor stops the step: 'no lighter option - the load holds')

title: Unknown step, insufficient data with a loaded reference
rule_basis: W-7: unknown step adds equipmentStep to missing, note 'steps cannot be computed'; 'no lighter option' printed only when the step is known
ambiguity_note: What conservative is printed with an unknown step is not stated: equal to recommend (R3 run-2 advisory says that is what happens, 'with no note') or omitted. Expected: no lower invented load; equal-to-recommend tolerated.

title: Unknown step, 2-for-2 positive history

expected.next_step_gist: growth needs a known equipment step

rule_basis: Design §4.1: unmet requirements -> missing + printed fallback, never a silent branch; W-16: unknown step -> no estimate
ambiguity_note: No rule says what growth does without a step (hold + missing is the cautious reading; a default per equipment would give +5). Conservative with unknown step unsettled as above.

title: Dumbbell per hand: 2-for-2 at 22 kg per hand

expected.next_step_gist: sets at 24 per hand in range

rule_basis: Design metric 9: dumbbell step 2 kg per hand; 2/22 = 9.1 % <= 10 % cap; loads stay per hand

title: Light dumbbell 8 kg per hand, 2-for-2 - step is 25 % of the load

expected.next_step_gist: progress by reps (step above the 10 % cap)

rule_basis: Design §3.3 Stage C 10 % cap / T1(f)

title: 10-day break after a 2-for-2 positive history (reason holiday)
rule_basis: 2-for-2 has no recovery condition; invariant 11(c) forbids growth only after a break >= return. Detraining literature: strength retained ~3 weeks (McMaster 2013, Bosquet 2013)
ambiguity_note: Design §5 table implies reasons other than deliberate deload may reduce at rest_with_question; with reason unknown (no answer) the rule text does not say whether 'one step lower' applies below 'return'.

title: 20-day break (return) after a 2-for-2 positive history, reason holiday
rule_basis: BR-038 return >= 14 d; T2(b) return ladder 2 rungs from 1 step below; invariant 11(c) no growth after a break >= return

title: 40-day break (rebuild), reason holiday

expected.next_step_gist: rebuild workout 1 of 3 -> back to 60 by the third

rule_basis: BR-038 rebuild >= 28 d; T2(b) 3 rungs from 2 steps below

title: 40-day break (rebuild), reason unknown
rule_basis: T2(b) + T4(g): two steps below plus one for unknown

title: Rebuild ladder after one successful return workout at 55
rule_basis: T4(f): a success (sets >= floor, RPE <= 8) advances the rung; rebuild 3 rungs from 2 steps below
ambiguity_note: Rung values are not written out: '3 rungs from 2 steps below' is read as 55 -> 57.5 -> 60. Also whether metric 4 now reads 55 (newest) as the working weight (item 4 / W-8) instead of 60 is unsettled during a ladder.

title: 100-day break (restart) with a loaded reference

expected.next_step_gist: restart: after this workout the rebuild ladder follows

rule_basis: Design §5 as amended: restart -> Stage A row 1, with a loaded reference the candidate is one step below it (W-4); no performance in 8 weeks -> insufficient
ambiguity_note: T2(b)/W-6 restart = cold start (no number), and Fix-S 'lower candidate wins - a cold start is lowest' could make the restart row win over W-4's number; review run-1 advisory notes the two paths disagree. Detraining after ~3 months (Mujika & Padilla 2000) supports reducing more than one step for strength; one step is optimistic. Non-monotonic: a 40-day rebuild starts 2 steps below (55), a 100-day restart via W-4 only 1 step below (57.5).

title: Insufficient data + rebuild tier: one performance at 40, 30 d ago

expected.next_step_gist: log it once - that performance becomes the reference

rule_basis: W-4: after a break tier (return/rebuild/restart) one step below the reference, tier named in the reason (not the tier's ladder depth)

title: Insufficient data with a loaded reference: one performance 40x10,10,9

expected.next_step_gist: log it once more - working weight follows

rule_basis: Item 3 / W-4 / BR-036

title: Insufficient data, tie on the most-used load: 40x10,40x10,45x8,45x8
rule_basis: W-4: most-used working load, heavier on a tie

title: No history at all (new exercise)

expected.next_step_gist: log this exercise once - that performance becomes the reference

rule_basis: W-4 / BR-036: no reference -> no number, no conservative; v12 forbids inventing one

title: Bodyweight pull-up, history without load
rule_basis: W-4: a reference with no loaded set (bodyweight) -> no number; design §3.4 bodyweight progresses by reps
ambiguity_note: Whether a bodyweight strength exercise with >= 2 performances goes through Stage A insufficient data (no number) or through the scheme on reps only (rep target, no load) is not stated; expected only pins 'no kg number'.

title: Plank (isometric) - non-strength
rule_basis: Load-plan T2(d): non-strength exercises print 'recommend: n/a for <type>'; design §3.4 isometric progresses by hold time

title: Leg press after session 1 only (110x12 x3), range 8-10
rule_basis: W-4: one performance -> reference load

title: Leg press after 110x3 -> 110,110,120,120, range 8-10
rule_basis: Item 4 / W-8 (AC-LPF-5): newest performance's highest load with all its sets >= floor = 120 > W-1 recurring 110; 2-for-2 at 120: 1 of 2; one-session: 12 < 13

title: Leg press after 110x3 -> 110,110,120,120, range 10-12
rule_basis: Item 4 / W-8; item 5 thresholds top+2 = 14, top+3 = 15

title: Leg press after 110,130,130,135 (owner full history), range 8-10
rule_basis: Item 4 / W-8 'leg press ... 135 after 09-27' (single set at 135 x12 reached the floor); 2-for-2 1 of 2; 12 < 13
ambiguity_note: W-8 records 135 'as ordered' from a single set; item 4 says '>= 130'. The literal rule gives 135. Literature-wise a single top set is a thin basis but 135x12 is above range in 8-10, so the load is demonstrated.

title: Leg press after 110,130,130,135 (owner full history), range 10-12
rule_basis: Item 4 / W-8; item 5

title: Newest session progressed: 60,60 then 65x9,9,8 (range 8-10)
rule_basis: Item 4 / W-8: newest performance's load whose sets all reached the floor wins over the recurring 60 (closes the R3 recency advisory)

title: Volume-only change: 5x10 @ 60 vs 3x10 @ 60 earlier
rule_basis: Item 8 / W-9: volume is printed, never a decision input

title: Barbell curl 20 kg, 2-for-2 positive - 2.5 kg step is 12.5 %

expected.next_step_gist: progress by reps (step above the 10 % cap)

rule_basis: Design §3.3 Stage C '≈ 10 %' cap / T1(f)
ambiguity_note: '≈ 10 %' - whether 12.5 % passes is not settled; strict reading holds at 20, a tolerant one grows to 22.5. NSCA lists 1-2 kg upper-body increments for small lifts, so 2.5 kg on 20 kg is the smallest practical bar increment.
